newsitem.title: CHINA: China says to merge loss-making airlines.
newsitem.headline: China says to merge loss-making airlines.

text.p: China will merge weaker companies in the aviation sector in a bid to stem losses and boost efficiency, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

It quoted Shen Yuankang, vice-minister of the General Administration of Civil Aviation of China, as telling a meeting of domestic airline officials on Saturday the sector would gradually streamline its operations.
China Northwest, based in the popular tourist destination of Xian in central China, and Nanjing Airlines were already cooperating to expand their market share, the agency said.

Chengdu Aircraft Repair was being combined with Southwest Airlines while a subsidiary of Northern Airlines and Heilongjiang Swan Air, both companies operating in the nation's economically ailing northeast, have already been consolidated.
It gave no further details of plans for mergers but it said that the effort to build up larger, more competitive companies was a focus of the airline industry meeting.
China began to break up what once was a single national airline in the 1980s and later allowed new entrants in the sector to spur competition.
Many regional governments have built new airports without guidance of central authorities, resulting in the duplication of services and other inefficiencies.
Rapid economic growth in recent years, particularly along the eastern and southeastern coastal regions, has spurred demand for air services.
That in turn has helped some of the nation's airlines, such as China Eastern and China Southern, which are based in Shanghai and the southern city of Guangzhou.
But vice-minister Shen said in August last year that all but six of China's 29 airlines were losing money.
